title: Our AI RPG remembers what you type — now we're stuck on how much freedom is too much
author: Pant0Mime3
selftext:
Hi! We're a small team building Melt Hollow, a browser RPG where you type what you want to do (or tap a suggested action) and the AI narrates how the world, NPCs and battles respond. [https://playmelt.com/](https://playmelt.com/)

The moment in the video is real gameplay: what you type to finish the prologue boss gets quoted back to you later by an NPC, as something you shouted in your sleep.

**Where we are**

Early players seem to enjoy the first few hours. NPCs can already generate new quests from conversations. Our next goal is a world that keeps expanding as you play: new quests, NPCs and places, generated on the fly.

**How it works**

Under the hood, every turn sends the player's text plus a world bible and quest state to an LLM, and our game logic turns its output into damage, items and quest progress.

**Where we're stuck**

1. **Freedom vs. guardrails.** If generation is too open, stories drift, break the setting, or just get boring. Too many templates and it stops feeling alive. We're leaning toward a lorebook-style world bible plus quest templates we keep refining. How are you handling this? Anything that worked, or failed badly?
2. **Players keep trying to tame monsters.** A surprising number of players try to befriend enemies instead of fighting them. Would you lean into emergent behavior like this (recruitable monsters), or protect the core loop?
3. **Measuring "fun."** Ideally, quests players enjoy would shape future generation. How would you even detect that? Completion rate, session length, how much players type?

Play free in your browser: [https://playmelt.com/](https://playmelt.com/)

We'd genuinely love your feedback, even "this won't work because...". If you're up for helping shape the game, please join our Discord. We're actively looking for players to tell us what works and what doesn't: [https://discord.gg/qZYqqVkT9H](https://discord.gg/qZYqqVkT9H)

Note: all art is AI-generated placeholder for this MVP. If the gameplay proves fun, we plan to commission human artists.

comments.author: OfficialJoeBroe
comments.body:
players trying to befriend enemies is a gift- they're telling you what they want. i'd let them, but gate it behind a quest or item so it feeds the loop instead of replacing combat

on drift, i'd let the model write flavor freely and keep anything that changes state (quest steps, items, who's alive) owned by your game logic. for fun i'd watch what people do unprompted, like coming back to talk to an npc, more than completion rate

replies.author: Pant0Mime3
replies.body: Thanks! On drift, that's close to what we do now: the model narrates, code owns damage, items and quest state. Gating befriending behind a quest is a great idea, and "coming back to an NPC unprompted" is exactly the fun metric we were missing.
